en.title: Total Requests After Daily Bulk Server Replacements
en.description:
There are initially n servers, and each server's ID is also the number of requests it handles. Over the next n days, on day j every server with ID replaced[j] changes its ID to newId[j]; output the sum of IDs after each day's operation. Replacing an ID that does not exist, or replacing an ID with itself, leaves the result unchanged.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by three lines of n integers each: the initial IDs, replaced, and newId. The raw ranges are written as 105 and 104 without superscripts; this site explicitly uses 1≤n≤100000 and 1≤every ID≤10000.
en.output: Output n integers, the total requests after each day's operation.
en.explanation: The answers are 40 2, 2 10 and 11 7 11; a replacement also affects servers whose IDs were already changed on an earlier day.
hints: Keep the ID frequencies and the total. When r changes to v, move c=count[r] over, apply total+=(v−r)*c, and output the updated total.
